title: Internal Hom computes morphisms of coherent completions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Modules, tensor pullback and direct image are on these ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Locally Noetherian means locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means additionally quasi-compact and quasi-separated (quasi-compact diagonal). Coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $X$ be Noetherian, let $J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be quasi-coherent, and let $F,G$ be coherent modules. Let $\mathcal H=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(F,G)$, the module sheaf of local module homomorphisms [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Then $\mathcal H$ is coherent, and its geometric-stalk support is contained in $\operatorname{Supp}(F)\cap\operatorname{Supp}(G)$ (the nonzero geometric-stalk loci). There is a canonical bijection, natural in $F,G$, $$\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\Gamma(X,\mathcal H/J^n\mathcal H)\ \simeq\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Coh}(X,J)}(\widehat F_J,\widehat G_J).$$ Here completions and the inverse-system category are [def-sfb-space-coherent-adic-system]. The composite of the quotient-section map from $\Gamma(X,\mathcal H)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(F,G)$ with this bijection sends $u$ to its quotient maps $(u\bmod J^n)_n$.

source.place: Tag 08B6 (lemma-completion-internal-hom); coherence and support of sheaf Hom as in the proof of Tag 08B9 (lemma-fully-faithful), first two paragraphs.

proof.text: Fix an etale scheme chart $e:U\to X$. Etale pullback is slice restriction [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the scheme comparison [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] writes $F|_U=A_U(F_U)$ and $G|_U=A_U(G_U)$ with coherent Zariski modules $F_U,G_U$, by the assumed coherence of $F,G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-local-finite-presentation], $F_U$ is finitely presented. Put $H_U=\mathcal Hom(F_U,G_U)$. This is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-sheaf-hom-coherent]. The Hom comparison [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-tensor-hom-comparison] identifies $A_U(H_U)$ with $\mathcal H|_U$: the latter restriction is exactly local module maps on the slice, by [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. These identifications are canonical under further chart restriction. Thus $\mathcal H$ is quasi-coherent (its presentations are local on the site) and has coherent chart pullbacks, proving coherence.

source.place: Tag 08B9 (lemma-fully-faithful), coherence paragraph; descent.tex Tag 06VE(8); modules.tex Tags 01BW and 01CQ.

proof.text: For a point $u\in U$, finite presentation gives $(H_U)_u=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{U,u}}((F_U)_u,(G_U)_u)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-internal-hom-finite-presentation]. If either input stalk is zero this Hom is zero. Hence $\operatorname{Supp}_U(H_U)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}_U(F_U)\cap\operatorname{Supp}_U(G_U)$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support] to the three quasi-coherent modules to identify these sets with inverse images of the three geometric-stalk supports on $X$. Choose a surjective atlas and refine its source by affine opens, as allowed by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Every point of $X$ has a point on such a chart above it, so the chartwise containment implies the asserted containment on $X$.

source.place: Tag 08B9 (lemma-fully-faithful), support paragraph; modules.tex Tag 01CP; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 07TY.

proof.text: Define the canonical map before proving bijectivity. Write $F_n=F/J^nF$, $G_n=G/J^nG$, and $H_n=\mathcal H/J^n\mathcal H$ [def-sfb-space-coherent-adic-system]. Postcomposition with $G\to G_n$ sends a local map $v:F\to G$ to $q^G_n v$. It kills $J^n\mathcal H$, since $q^G_n(av)=a(q^G_n v)=0$ for $a\in J^n$. Every local map $F\to G_n$ kills $J^nF$ by the same identity. The two sheaf cokernel universal properties therefore give $\epsilon_n:H_n\to\mathcal Hom(F_n,G_n)$, uniquely characterized by $\epsilon_n(\bar v)(\bar x)=\overline{v(x)}$ on local lifts [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Restrictions preserve these equations; reduction from level $m$ to $n\le m$ sends both sides to the same class modulo $J^n$. A compatible family of global sections consequently gives maps $F_n\to G_n$ commuting with every transition, hence a system morphism. Call this map $\Phi$.

source.place: Tag 08B6 (lemma-completion-internal-hom), canonical map made explicit by the quotient universal properties; coherent.tex Tag 0882.

proof.text: On a Noetherian affine etale chart $U$, let $J_U$ be the quasi-coherent Zariski ideal corresponding to $J|_U$. The exact comparison [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] and tensor comparison [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-tensor-hom-comparison] identify $A_U(J_U^nP)$ with $(J|_U)^nA_U(P)$ and identify the quotient maps for $P=F_U,G_U,H_U$. The tensor terms, products and quotients are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections, lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], so the exact comparison applies. Indeed each product is the image of $J_U^{\otimes n}\otimes P\to P$; the exact functor preserves that image, and the tensor comparison preserves its multiplication map. Cokernels then give the quotient identification, including transitions. Full faithfulness of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies maps between the quotients and thus compatible families of such maps. Its identity comparison on open sections identifies $H_n(U)$ with $\Gamma(U,H_U/J_U^nH_U)$. The map $\Phi_U$ is exactly the canonical scheme map: both take a locally lifted $v$ to $\bar x\mapsto\overline{v(x)}$. The scheme theorem [lem-weil-pbc-completion-internal-hom], with its two arguments exchanged, proves $\Phi_U$ bijective. Here $U$ is Noetherian because it is affine and locally Noetherian by the assumed local Noetherianity of $X$ on etale charts. All its other hypotheses are exactly the coherent chart modules and quasi-coherent ideal just specified.

source.place: Tag 08B6 (lemma-completion-internal-hom), reduction to schemes; coherent.tex Tag 0882; descent.tex Tag 06VE(5),(7),(8).

proof.text: Injectivity of $\Phi$ follows by restricting two families with the same image to each Noetherian affine etale chart and using the injectivity of $\Phi_U$ from step 4. At every level the sections are equal on a covering family, hence equal by the sheaf condition. Affine charts cover every scheme object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$; equality there is equality of global sections. Here global sections can be read as compatible families on all scheme objects, so no terminal scheme object for $X$ is required.

For surjectivity let $t=(t_n)$ be a morphism of the two completion systems. On each affine etale chart $U$ use step 4 to obtain its unique inverse family $s_{U,n}\in H_n(U)$. For two charts $U,V$, their fibre product over $X$ is a scheme by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]; cover it by affine opens $W$. Each $W\to X$ is again etale, and is Noetherian because it is affine and locally Noetherian. The restrictions of the two families to $W$ both map to $t|_W$ under $\Phi_W$, since step 3 defined $\Phi$ using restriction-compatible quotient maps. Local injectivity implies they coincide. The sheaf condition for $H_n$ therefore glues these sections, for each $n$, to a global $s_n$. On every chart its reduction to level $n$ agrees with $s_{U,n}$, so the glued family is transition-compatible. Likewise $\epsilon_n(s_n)=t_n$ can be checked on the charts. Thus $\Phi(s)=t$. Gluing on any other scheme object is obtained by base changing the covering charts and taking affine refinements, so these are genuine global sections on the small etale site.

source.place: Tag 08B6 (lemma-completion-internal-hom), etale descent expanded as gluing of sections and component morphisms; no effectivity theorem for new objects is needed.

proof.text: Finally the quotient-section family of a global morphism $u:F\to G$ has at level $n$ the class of $u$ in $H_n$. By the defining equation in step 3 its image is $\bar x\mapsto\overline{u(x)}$, exactly the quotient map of the completion functor [def-sfb-space-coherent-adic-system]. For $a:F'\to F$ and $b:G\to G'$, both routes around the naturality square send a local representative $v$ to the map $\bar x\mapsto\overline{b(v(a(x)))}$. Local representatives suffice because quotient projections are epimorphisms of sheaves. Thus the square commutes at each level and on compatible families. Bijectivity then gives the asserted natural bijection and its normalization.

source.place: Tag 08B6 (lemma-completion-internal-hom), naturality and completion-map normalization of the canonical quotient construction.
